events.title: Arrest of the Knights Templar in France
events.description: On Friday, October 13, 1307, King Philip IV of France ordered the mass arrest of members of the Knights Templar throughout France, including the Grand Master Jacques de Molay. The knights were accused of heresy, blasphemy, and other charges, and many were tortured into confessions.
events.significance: The arrests led to the dissolution of the powerful Templar order by Pope Clement V in 1312 and are often cited as an origin of the superstition surrounding Friday the 13th.

events.title: Cornerstone of the White House Laid
events.description: The cornerstone of the Executive Mansion in Washington, D.C., later known as the White House, was laid on October 13, 1792. The building was designed by Irish-born architect James Hoban.
events.significance: The White House became the official residence and workplace of the President of the United States and a lasting symbol of American government.

events.title: Italy Declares War on Germany
events.description: On October 13, 1943, the Italian government under Marshal Pietro Badoglio declared war on Nazi Germany, a month after Italy's armistice with the Allies. Italy was thereby recognized as a co-belligerent of the Allied powers.
events.significance: The declaration marked Italy's formal switch of sides in World War II and contributed to the Allied campaign in the Italian peninsula.

events.title: Birth of Margaret Thatcher
events.description: Margaret Thatcher, born Margaret Hilda Roberts on October 13, 1925, in Grantham, England, became the first woman to serve as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, holding office from 1979 to 1990.
events.significance: Thatcher was a defining figure of late 20th-century politics whose free-market policies, known as Thatcherism, reshaped the British economy and influenced conservative politics worldwide.

events.title: Greenwich Adopted as Prime Meridian
events.description: On October 13, 1884, the International Meridian Conference in Washington, D.C., voted to adopt the meridian passing through Greenwich, England, as the world's prime meridian for longitude and timekeeping.
events.significance: The decision standardized global navigation and time zones, forming the basis for Greenwich Mean Time and modern world timekeeping.
